Bring gently to the boil, stirring occasionally, then reduce heat and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Meanwhile, tip the blueberries into a pan with 1 tsp of water and honey and gently poach until the blueberries have thawed and are tender, but still holding their shape.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blueberries.

title: Easter Chick Cupcakes
description: Celebrate Easter with these adorable Easter Chick Cupcakes. These delightful treats will bring joy to your festivities and are suitable for a renal diet.
steps: To make the cupcakes
Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C Fan/Gas Mark 4.
To make the cupcakes
In a bowl, combine the flour and bicarbonate of soda.
To make the cupcakes
In a separate bowl, beat the egg, gradually add the sugar, vanilla extract and oil, and stir until combined.
To make the cupcakes
Add the flour mixture and half a bottle of Renastep (approx. 60ml) and whisk.
To make the cupcakes
Add the remaining half a bottle of Renastep to the mixture and whisk.
To make the cupcakes
Place the 4 x 8 cm diameter cupcake cases into a muffin tray and evenly pour the cake mixture into the cases.
To make the cupcakes
Bake in the oven for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown.
To make the cupcakes
Carefully transfer the cupcakes onto a wire rack to cool
For the frosting
Cream together the butter and icing sugar in a bowl.
For the frosting
Add half a bottle of Renastep (approx. 60ml) and the vanilla extract to the butter icing mixture and mix well.
For the frosting
Add the food colouring to get your desired colour.
To decorate
Spread the icing onto the surface of the four cupcakes evenly, using the back of a spoon.
To decorate
Dip the surface of the cupcakes into the coconut.
To decorate
Add the ‘eyes’ to each cupcake using 2 chocolate chips.
To decorate

title: Baklava
description: Learn how to make this delicious homemade baklava with pecans, hazelnuts, and a citrusy syrup. Crispy, nutty, and sweet - ready in just over an hour!
steps: Preheat the oven to 200˚C /180˚C fan / Gas Mark 6.
In a bowl, combine chopped pecans, pumpkin seeds, hazelnuts, cinnamon and cardamom with the honey.
Place a sheet of filo pastry into a 25x15cm baking tray and brush with butter. Continue this process until half the pack of pastry has been used.
Spread the nut mixture evenly over the pastry.
Place the other half of filo sheets on top of the nut mixture, continuing the buttering and layering process until the whole pack is used. Any remaining butter should be poured over the top.
Cut 12 portions into the baklava and bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Meanwhile, place the sugar and water into a pan with orange zest. Bring the syrup to a boil and then allow to simmer until it resembles runny honey.
Remove the baklava from the oven and pour all of the syrup over evenly.
Allow to cool fully before serving.

title: Vegetable Sambusa
description: Make this crispy kidney-friendly vegetable sambusa filled with spiced carrots, cauliflower, peas, and peppers to have as a savoury snack. Cooks in 20 minutes
steps: Heat oil in a pan and fry the onions, garlic and ginger until soft.
Once softened add in the cumin, garam masala and coriander, mix together for 2 minutes.
Then add in the carrots, cauliflower, peppers, and peas, stir together, and cook until soft. Set aside.
In a small bowl mix together the flour and water until a paste forms.
Place a small spoonful of the vegetable mixture onto 1 spring roll wrapper, Fold over the mixture and continue to fold in opposite directions until a triangle has formed.
Spread a small amount of the flour mixture at the opening of the triangle and press together to seal.
Heat enough oil in a pan to shallow fry (usually ¼ inch up the side of the pan). Test the temperature with a small amount of pastry, if it turns golden brown and bubbles, the oil is ready to fry.
Place the sambusa into the pan and cook on both sides until golden brown, remove from the pan and place onto kitchen paper.
Once slightly cooled serve and enjoy!

title: Rice Bukhari
steps: Preheat an oven to 180°C/356°F/Gas mark 4.
Onto a baking tray add the carrots and red pepper, drizzle with a little oil, and roast for 20-30 minutes or until soft.
Heat 1/2 the oil in a pan and add cloves and cardamom pods, allow to toast slightly.
Add onions, garlic, and allow to soften slightly.
Once softened, add in the chicken pieces and allow to brown slightly on all sides.
Once browned, add in the cinnamon, allspice, white pepper, dried lime powder, nutmeg, coriander, and cumin. Stir until the chicken is fully coated with the spices.
Remove the red pepper and carrots from the oven and add to a blender with enough stock to cover the vegetables and form a thin puree.
Blend until smooth and then add into the pan with the rest of the vegetable stock, stir well, and bring to boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and allow to simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add in the rice and cook for 10 minutes or until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Once cooked, place the rice on a plate and add the chicken on top and set aside.
Add the butter to a pan and melt, add in the macadamia nuts and pumpkin seeds and cook until slightly brown.
Pour the butter and nuts over the rice, serve and enjoy.

title: Chicken Nuggets
description: Make this homemade version of chicken nuggets, created with renal patients in mind. They are super quick to make in just 15 minutes. Try it today!
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts, chopped into bite-size pieces
80g breadcrumbs (buy ready-made or grate some bread)
steps: Put the breadcrumbs in a bowl.
Put the yoghurt in a separate bowl.
Dip the raw chicken pieces into the yoghurt then coat in the breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry in oil (try rapeseed/sunflower oil) for about 5 minutes each side, but keep an eye on them to make sure they don’t start to burn!
hints: Add 2 tsp of sage for added flavour.
Serve these with polenta chips or chopped up into hot pasta with a knob of garlic butter.

description: Try these kidney-friendly Egg Muffins recipe from My Renal Nutrition, designed for individuals with renal disease, offering a nutritious and delicious meal option.
steps: Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan and fry broccoli and peppers with paprika and black pepper until soft.
Whisk eggs and Renastep in a bowl until fully combined.
Pour egg mixture evenly between each muffin cup.
Evenly distribute the cooked vegetables and crumbled feta between each muffin.
Bake for 15 minutes or until cooked through and serve.

title: Pea courgette purée
description: This recipes makes one portion of weaning suitable food which takes just 20 minutes to make and can have a thin consistency if required.
ingredients: 100ml of breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialized low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian)
steps: Cut the courgettes into small chunks.
Boil the courgette for 5 minutes.
Add frozen peas and boil for a further 3-4 minutes.
Drain vegetables and cool.
Add 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian).
Use a blender to whizz up to a purée consistency.
Add more breast milk, standard infant formula or the specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed if a thinner consistency is required.

title: Easy Chicken Pizza
description: Discover an easy, nutritious chicken pizza recipe suitable for those on a renal diet. Try this delicious meal option which you can make in 15 minutes.
ingredients: 4 chunks of either french bread, pitta or wraps
100g of tinned (no added salt) or frozen sweetcorn
steps: Preheat oven to 180ºC/160ºC Fan/350ºF/Gas 4. Cover a baking tray with greaseproof paper, and place either the French bread, pitta or wraps on top.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, then add the corn, red peppers, chicken and garlic. Fry for a further 2 minutes, until thoroughly cooked through. Remove from the heat and stir in the tomato puree.
Share out the chicken mixture evenly between bases then top with a blob of cream cheese and grated cheddar cheese.
Bake in the oven for 3-5 minutes or until the cheese melts and the base goes slightly crisp. Remove from the oven and sprinkle each pizza with the chopped basil.
hints: Serve with polenta fries, rice or pasta.

title: Butternut squash and broccoli purée
description: Try this weaning recipe which can be part of your baby's first foods. Step-by-step recipe for Butternut squash & broccoli purée!
ingredients: 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian)
Other vegetables you could add with butternut squash include carrots, peas or spinach
steps: Peel the butternut squash, scoop out the middle and chop into small pieces.
Chop the broccoli into small pieces.
Boil the butternut squash for approximately 8-10 minutes.
Add the broccoli to cook for a further 5 minutes.
Drain water and allow vegetables to cool.
Add 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian).

title: Simit Bread
description: Try this kidney-friendly Simit bread recipe – a soft, sesame-crusted Turkish classic made with low-sodium ingredients and perfect for everyday enjoyment
ingredients: 135g Strong white bread flour (a little extra flour will be needed for dusting)
½ tbsp Pomegranate molasses or molasses syrup
steps: Warm the Renastep gently in a pan to no more than 30˚C. Meanwhile, mix the flour and sugar in a bowl.
Add the dried yeast and Renastep and mix well until a soft dough is formed.
Place the dough onto a clean work surface dusted with flour. Knead the dough for for 5 minutes until the dough feels stretchy.
Place the dough in a clean bowl, cover and leave to prove for an hour, until doubled in size.
Heat oven to 200˚C/180˚C fan/gas mark 6.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan for 2-3 minutes until golden and set aside.
Mix the pomegranate molasses or molasses syrup with 50ml water in a shallow bowl.
When the dough has risen, roll out onto a clean, dusted work surface into a sausage shape about 45cm long and cut in half.
Place the two pieces lengthways together continuously twist them over each other for the full length of dough. Cut the twist into 2 equal pieces. Brush both sides with the molasses water.

Pour the toasted sesame seeds onto a piece of parchment paper and roll each twist of dough through the seeds until well covered. On a baking tray, join the ends of each twist to form two circles, cover and leave to prove for another 10 minutes.
When the bread has risen, uncover and bake for 15-18 mins until golden. Allow to cool before serving.

Allow to gently simmer for 1 hour, stirring regulatory to ensure it does not stick or burn.
Once the rice is cooked, stir in the vanilla essence and cinnamon.

description: This kidney-friendly Alu Sabudana Tikki recipe is made with sago, potatoes, and mild spices making a low-sodium snack. It takes just 20 minutes to cook.
steps: Wash sago (2-3 times) and soak for 6-7 hours or overnight. Once soaked, drain and rinse again.
Boil potatoes for 10 minutes, drain and grate them. Mix sago with grated potatoes and set aside.
To the mixture add ginger, garlic, turmeric and chilli powder (optional).
Add 1 tsp arrowroot/cornflour and mix all of it well to form a soft dough.
Grease hand with oil and prepare ball-sized tikki (patty).
Shallow fry in hot oil. Roast on low flame until it turns golden brown.
Flip over and cook on both sides.

title: Shai paneer
description: Learn how to make this creamy shahi paneer in a rich, flavourful, spiced cashew-tomato dish - perfect with naan or rice, made with Renastep.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and add in the almonds, cashews and cardamom pods, fry until golden and remove from pan.
Add in the ginger, garlic, green chilli and onions and cook until soft.
Add everything into a blender and blend to a smooth paste, some water may be added to achieve a smoother consistency.
In the same pan heat oil and add in the cumin seeds, cinnamon stick and cloves and allow to sizzle for 30 seconds.
Then add in the garam masala, turmeric and nut paste and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add in the water and bubble for around 10 minutes.

Add the sugar, cornflour and rose water and whisk continuously for 3-4 minutes until the mixture starts to thicken.
Remove from the heat (it will continue to thicken when chilled).
Line a bowl with cling film and pour the mixture in.
Let the mixture cool at room temperature for 30 minutes, then transfer to the fridge and chill for 2-3 hours or overnight if possible.
When chilled, loosen the cling film, and flip the pudding over on to plate.

title: Double-Boiled Wedges and Aioli
ingredients: 350g red skin potatoes, peeled and sliced into wedges
steps: Boil the potatoes in a large amount of water for 10 minutes, this helps the potato lose some of its potassium.
Pour away the water.
Now boil the potatoes in fresh water for a further 10 minutes and again pour away the water once the potatoes are cooked. This lowers the potassium content even further.
Always ensure to pour away the water. The water should not be used for sauces or cooking other ingredients.
Once drained, place the wedges onto a baking tray, drizzle with vegetable oil, mixed herbs and black pepper.
Bake for 20 – 25 minutes or until golden brown.
While baking mix together the mayonnaise and garlic until well combined, place into a small bowl and set aside.
Once cooked serve the wedges immediately with the aioli and enjoy!

title: Pierogi (Polish Dumplings)
description: Discover how to make our take on Pierogi the moreish Polish dumplings, for those on a renal diet. This recipe takes 20 minutes to cook and makes 4 portions.
steps: To make the dough
Place the flour into a bowl and make a ‘well’ in the middle. Add the egg, melted butter and hot water.
To make the dough
Mix together until a dough forms.
To make the dough
Turn onto a board and knead dough until smooth. Roll into a ball, cover and set aside for 20 minutes.
To make the filling
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and add the minced garlic and chopped onion. Fry until the onions become translucent.
To make the filling
Add in the minced beef and fry until browned.
To make the filling
Add in the grated carrot, black pepper and oregano and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Assembly
Roll out dough into a 10” (25cm) to 11” (28cm) circle. Cut 12 circles in the dough with a 3” (8cm) round cookie cutter.
Assembly
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of each dough circle. Fold over, stretch and press sides together to form a crescent-shaped dumpling
Assembly
In a large saucepan of boiling water, carefully place two or three dumplings in the water. The pierogi will float to the top when done. Remove with a slotted spoon and place onto kitchen paper.
Assembly
Once boiled, lightly fry the pierogi in the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil over a medium heat. Fry for 3 minutes on each side until crispy and golden brown.
Creamy Cheese Sauce
In a pan, on a low heat add the Renastep, cream cheese, mixed herbs and garlic powder and stir until combined.
Creamy Cheese Sauce
Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened (do not boil).
Creamy Cheese Sauce
Divide the cheese sauce over the 4 portions of Pierogi.

title: Gingery Cookies
description: Try baking our deliciously spiced Gingery Cookies recipe, perfect for anyone who loves a warm, flavorful treat. This easy recipe makes 18 cookies.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C Fan/350° F/Gas 4.
In a large bowl, cream together the butter and sugar.
Add the golden syrup and dry ingredients and beat to combine.
Once everything is combined, using your hands (make sure they are clean!) roll the mixture out into little balls, keeping each even in size.
Place 3cm apart on a greased baking tray and lightly press down using a fork.
Bake in the oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Hünkar Beğendi
description: Cook this kidney-friendly Hünkar Beğendi recipe with tender turkey in tomato sauce served over creamy roasted aubergine purée to make a delicious meal.
steps: Place the aubergines under a hot grill and allow to char on all sides, remove from the grill and allow to cool.
Once cooled peel the aubergines charred skin and set aside.
Heat oil and flour in a pan and stir to form a paste.
Add the roasted aubergines to the pan, once heated mash the aubergines to form a smooth paste.
Reduce the heat and gradually add in the Renastep, black pepper and nutmeg to the mixture and stir well until combined.
Allow to cook for a further 2 minutes and then set aside.
In a separate pan, heat oil in a pan and add in the turkey chunks. Allow to cook until browned.
Add the onions and peppers to the meat and cook until softened.
Add in the grated tomato mixture and the additional water, allow to cook until the sauce has reduced and the meat is fully cooked.
Serve on top of the roasted aubergine puree and serve.

steps: Heat water in a pan. When it’s boiling, add rice and cook for 10 minutes and set aside

Heat a small amount of oil in a frying pan and add the coated tofu. Cook until golden brown all over and set aside.
Heat oil in a frying pan and add garlic, harissa, black beans, and ½ the lime juice. Allow to fry until hot and then set aside.
For the pico de gallo add red pepper, onion and coriander to a small bowl. Stir well and set aside.
In a blender, add the peas, lime juice, and olive oil and blend until combined but still retaining some texture
Serve rice into a bowl and top with the tofu, black beans, pico de gallo, pea guacamole and coconut yoghurt. Sprinkle with coriander and serve!
